notes: Kelley & VerPlanck's Transit Center District Survey, read in full: the 74-page context statement, the DPR 523 D district record for the proposed New Montgomery, Mission & Second Historic District, and the three appendix tables. Facts come from three places and the citation locator says which: the narrative, the DPR district record's contributor and non-contributor tables, and the appendix tables of individually significant properties and existing survey ratings.

coverage.remaining: None. The document was read end to end; nothing in it is outstanding.
coverage.note: Read the whole 95-page file — a 74-page context statement, the DPR 523 D district record for the proposed New Montgomery, Mission & Second Historic District, and three appendix tables — and took 316 address-level facts across 171 distinct number-and-street combinations, every one of them carrying a street number. They come from four places: the appendix table of existing survey ratings (170 rows, block and lot given for each), the district record's tables of 86 contributors and 33 non-contributors (address, APN, construction date, property type and status codes), the appendix table of 24 individually significant properties outside the district, and the narrative. Never candidates, and so not recorded: 10 parking-lot and vacant-parcel rows that carry no building and no date, 5 of them addressed '000'; the 42 rows the ratings table marks '(Demo)', where the survey is recording a building already gone; buildings the narrative gives only by corner (the Selby Shot Tower at 1st and Howard, the Donahue gas works at 1st and Howard, the Grand Opera House at 3rd and Mission, the Union Hall on Howard between 3rd and 4th); and the Methodist Episcopal church at 645 Howard Street and the residential hotels at 362 and 315 Howard Street and 715 Howard Street, which are named with numbers but no date.
